p-queue (the PQueue class in source/index.ts, its options in source/options.ts) has a throwOnTimeout option, accepted by the constructor and by each add(), and false by default: when a task's timeout elapses, its promise resolves with undefined instead of rejecting, so a caller cannot tell a timed-out task from one that returned nothing, and add() is typed Promise<TaskResultType | void>. Remove the option, so that a timeout always rejects. With const queue = new PQueue({timeout: 300}): queue.add(async () => { await delay(400); return '🐌'; }) must reject with p-timeout's TimeoutError (today it resolves with undefined); a task that takes 200 ms must resolve with its value; queue.add(task, {timeout: 10}) for a task that takes 100 ms must reject with TimeoutError; and queue.add(task, {timeout: 500}) for a task that takes 400 ms must resolve with its value. A timed-out task emits the queue's error event with the TimeoutError and no completed event, and addAll() rejects when one of its tasks times out. Remove throwOnTimeout from the option types in source/options.ts and from the class, together with the add() and addAll() overloads that depended on it, so that add() is typed Promise<TaskResultType> and addAll() Promise<TaskResultsType[]> (for const queue = new PQueue(), queue.add(async () => '🦄') is Promise<string>). A throwOnTimeout that is still passed at run time is ignored: the timeout rejects all the same. What must not change: a task without a timeout runs to completion however long it takes; setting queue.timeout applies to the tasks added after it; a per-task timeout given to add() overrides the queue's; any other error from a task rejects its promise and emits error as today; after a timeout the queue goes on with the next tasks within its concurrency; and onIdle(), pending, size and priorities behave as today. Some existing tests in test/basic.ts and test/advanced.ts and the type test test-d/index.test-d.ts pass throwOnTimeout or expect a timed-out task to resolve; they describe the behaviour being removed, so change them to the new behaviour, keeping their other assertions. Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npm test (xo, then node --test over test/*.ts through tsx, then tsc and tsd).

Allowed changes: implementation code, and regression tests for the change (new test files, or new cases added to existing test files, in the project's own test directory and style).

Do not delete or weaken existing tests: keep every existing assertion (it may move to another test file), add no skip, only or todo markers, and add no coverage-ignore pragmas. A change that does any of these is rejected at evaluation whatever else passes.
